commits.message:
fix(console): end belongs to text; a renderable ends its own lines (rich-console-dcg)

Two consecutive prints of a Panel, Table or Rule left a blank line between
them: the renderable closed its last line and print then appended `end`
regardless.

The ticket framed the choice as an intended aesthetic or a column-tracking
console, and described Python Rich as the second. Rich 15.0.0 is neither. It
attaches `sep` and `end` only to runs of text items and lets any other
renderable own its line breaks. Column tracking would also have been wrong:
`print("a\n")` is "a\n\n" in Rich and must stay so, and only the item's kind,
not the cursor column, separates that trailing break from a Panel's.

Console.print now builds a PrintBlock list. A run of adjacent text items
(strings, RichText, data) is joined by `sep` and ended by `end`. Any other
renderable is a block whose lines are each closed by the print. This also
fixes the mixed cases, which matched Rich in none of these ways before:
`print("a", panel, "b")` put the panel's top edge on the "a" line and led
"b" with a space, and `end` was appended after a renderable.

One deliberate divergence from Rich remains: a renderable that leaves its last
line open, such as Strip, has it closed here, so the next print and the
export start on a new line.

Line ends added by print stay outside the print and console styles, as Rich
emits them.

Docs: docs/console.md gains a "Line ends" section. The blank line drawn in
docs/group.md and explained in docs/pretty.md is gone.

fix(columns): a declared column width yields to a narrower offer (rich-table-width-y1a) (#143)

* fix(columns): a declared column width yields to a narrower offer (rich-table-width-y1a)

`new Columns(items, { width: 6 })` rendered at `maxWidth: 3` laid out one
six-cell column and emitted six-cell lines into a three-cell request, while
`measure` already reported three. The terminal soft-wraps an oversized line and
the wrap takes the frame of everything printed after it.

`Columns._declaredWidth(options)` bounds the declared width by the offer, and
both `_divide` (render) and `_naturalWidth` (measure) read it, the same shape
`Table._outerWidth` gave the Table half of this ticket in #79. A declared width
is now what a column asks for, not what it takes, across both renderables.

The width sweep gains "Columns at a declared width" and "Columns at a declared
unbounded width", and the header note that excluded declared-width Columns is
deleted. Without the fix those two configurations and the new pinned test in
columns.test.ts fail (5 tests); with it the suite is green.

docs/tables.md said a declared `width` was a "Fixed total width — disables
auto-sizing, and overrides a container narrower than it". Neither half is true
on master: the container wins, and a declared width is a ceiling the table sizes
to its content within — five cells of content under `width: 40` render at five
unless `expand` is set (verified unchanged back to before #77). "Narrow widths"
now states that contract once, and the Sizing row links to it.
docs/columns.md gains the `width` row it never had.

Filed, not fixed here: rich-columns-awe (Columns `expand` and `padding` are
accepted and never applied) and rich-table-width-5cj (whether a declared Table
width should imply `expand`, as it does in upstream Rich).

* docs(table): name the table's rendered width, not its content's, in the declared-width example (rich-table-width-y1a)
